input: Freeze a batch of homemade stock this week

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The type of stock (chicken, beef, vegetable, fish, etc.) determines ingredients, cook time, and yield — the whole recipe changes.
Whether this is for one person, a family, or meal-prep for many determines how large a batch to make and how to portion it for freezing.
Whether the stock still needs to be made from scratch or is already cooked and just needs to be frozen changes what steps are actually left to do.
Available freezer space is a hard limit that directly caps the batch size and the number or size of containers used.
The portioning format (ice cube trays, quart bags, mason jars, deli containers) affects how the stock is used later and how it should be packaged now.
Whether the user wants a rich, long-simmered stock or a quicker version affects the method, equipment, and time commitment required.
Knowing the intended use (soups, sauces, grains, drinking broth) determines concentration level, seasoning, and how 'done well' is judged.

gold.taskTitle: Freeze a batch of homemade stock this week
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to make and freeze a batch of homemade stock sometime this week.

questions.title: What type of stock are you planning to make?
questions.description: Identify the base — chicken, beef, vegetable, fish, bone broth, etc. — to shape the recipe, ingredients, and simmer time.

questions.title: How many people will this stock serve?
questions.description: Determine whether this is for a single household, meal-prepping for a crowd, or another scale, to set the right batch size.

questions.title: Is the stock already made, or does it still need cooking?
questions.description: Establish the current stage of the task — whether the remaining work is only freezing, or the full cook-and-freeze process.

questions.title: How much freezer space do you have available right now?
questions.description: Understand the hard storage limit to plan a realistic batch size and choose appropriate container sizes.

questions.title: What containers do you plan to freeze the stock in?
questions.description: Clarify the portioning format — ice cube trays, zip-lock bags, mason jars, or deli containers — to guide packaging steps.

questions.title: Do you want a quick stock or a long slow-simmered one?
questions.description: Determine the user's preferred method and time investment, which affects equipment needed and scheduling within the week.

questions.title: What will you mainly use this frozen stock for?
questions.description: Identify the primary end use — soups, sauces, cooking grains, sipping — to inform the ideal concentration and seasoning level.
